$Comment: MMO Skill Tree's half of the Christmas Set, Christmas_Set.json. Joins adds this file to that set instead
of making a set of its own, so the player still sees one Christmas Set entry. The set's name and members
stay that file's, so this file names none.
Its first two tiers ask exactly what the set's two tiers ask (Armor 2, then Armor 4), so each joins its
twin: its stats apply beside the set's. The third asks the same four pieces but binds its stats with
While, and a bound tier never joins another, so it is added as a tier of its own with a notice of its
own: the full-set line (tier_full) sits on it, and the unbound Armor 4 twin carries no line, so the
player reads each line once. A tier asking for something else would be added the same way. Requires
takes this file out on a server without MMO Skill Tree, where these stats do not exist and its lines
would name a bonus nobody gets; always write it with Min 1.
TrackGain_Woodcutting raises the Woodcutting XP the wearer earns and GatherYield the chance of a bonus
find on a gathering break, the luck Woodcutting's lucky rolls read, both in whole percent points (10 is
10%). The yield is the luck of chopping trees, so it counts only while a hatchet is in hand: While is
CommonLib's ZigHolding with Items naming the tools Woodcutting's own skill file lists (*Tool_Hatchet_*,
a name read along each item's Parent line, so a copy of a vanilla hatchet counts too). It names no MMO
Skill Tree condition on purpose: this pack depends on MMO Skill Tree only optionally, and a condition
nobody registered fails the file's read before Requires can drop it. The yield also raises the Winter
Bauble find while Christmas runs (Factors/SeasonsOfOrbis/Christmas_Bauble_Luck.json). Both stats are
Additive on purpose: these channels have a base of zero, so a Multiplicative entry computes nothing.
